contests.scopeNote: Only voters residing in Country Run Special Dependent Tax District vote on this referendum.

provenance.quote:
Referendum to Increase the Special Assessment of Country Run
Special District from $50 to $75
Referéndum para Incrementar el Impuesto del Distrito Especial de
Country Run de $50 a $75
In order to continue existing and future maintenance needs, shall the
Board of Trustees of Country Run Special Tax District increase the
future assessed tax from $50 to $75 and authorize at their discretion
to increase the tax by $25 per year in subsequent years, not to
exceed $200?

sources.reviewedEvidence: Actual official November 3, 2026 ALL RACES SAMPLE BALLOT. Complete 30 local candidate-office blocks contain 67 printed names. Lake St. Charles Seat 2 retains all three printed names as source history, while a newer withdrawal notice leaves two active choices. Four local questions include the three already-held county questions and the newly prepared precisely scoped Country Run question.
Official 2026 general election withdrawal notice: votes for Yvonne Brown and Toni Kristina Rhodus count; a vote for Barbara A. Kirby will not count. This is a notice, not a replacement sample ballot.

Official 2026 Community Development District Supervisor fact sheet explicitly states the electorate is all Hillsborough County registered voters residing in the district, nonpartisan, four-year terms. Seat number is an office within the CDD; no geographic seat subdivision is asserted.

Native official HTML notice despite local .pdf filename: Country Run referendum appears on the 2026 general ballot only for voters residing inside the Country Run Special Dependent Tax District. Exact question agrees with actual master sample.
County government explicitly identifies Commission Districts 5 and 7 as countywide. Districts 1 and 3 remain precise single districts.
Official 2026 School Board fact sheet explicitly labels Districts 2 and 4 single-member and District 6 countywide; four-year term. No school district subdivision inferred from candidate residence.
Official city current November 3, 2026 municipal election page gives the five qualified candidates for three city council positions, matching the county actual sample.
Official current On the Ballot page links actual 2026 general All Races Sample Ballot, distinct from personal voter lookup.
Official current Public Notices page directly links the Lake St. Charles withdrawal notice, Country Run referendum notice, and sample ballot legal notice.

Official local certification supplemental history, not a sample ballot. Explicitly says a sole nonpartisan candidate will not appear on ballot. Certified-only unopposed fields are kept separately from actual printed general choices. Special dependent trustees are documented separately as August primary offices.

Official Department of State certification for Hillsborough, August 28, 2026. Named WRI filings are preserved separately and are not inserted as ordinary printed local candidates. Existing statewide/federal/judicial fields remain untouched.
Official Special District Trustees 2026 fact sheet states August 18 primary election, distinguishing those certified dependent-district trustee lists from general ballot contests.

Additional actual official general-election all-races sample legal notice facsimile. Replays all 30 local candidate office blocks and all 67 printed names, including the three printed Lake St. Charles Seat 2 names. Withdrawal notice controls active choice status.
